diagram.manim_description: Draw a geometry-box protractor as printed on the NCERT page. Its centre O is the middle of its straight base and its outer radius is R; every size below is a fraction of R, with x to the right, y upward and O at the origin. Body: a half-disc of radius R (the part with y >= 0) filled CELL_FILL with a GUIDE outline of 2 px; under the base line a flat strip from x = -R to x = +R and from y = 0 down to y = -0.07 R, filled CELL_FILL with a GUIDE outline; the base line y = 0 from x = -0.67 R to x = +0.67 R is drawn in INK 2 px. Centre cut-out: a half-disc of radius 0.25 R centred at O, filled BG, with a GUIDE outline. Tick ring: 181 GUIDE ticks at 0, 1, 2 ... 180 degrees measured anticlockwise from the right end of the base, each pointing inward from the rim radius R: length 0.03 R at every 1 degree, 0.05 R at every multiple of 5 degrees and 0.09 R at every multiple of 10 degrees. Scale arcs: three GUIDE semicircle arcs of radius 0.91 R, 0.79 R and 0.67 R. Outer scale numbers: the 19 numbers 0, 10, 20 ... 180 in INK, each centred at radius 0.85 R and rotated to follow the arc; the outer scale reads 0 at the left end of the base and 180 at the right end, so the number n sits at (180 - n) degrees measured anticlockwise from the right end. Inner scale numbers: the 19 numbers 0, 10, 20 ... 180 in INK, each centred at radius 0.73 R and rotated to follow the arc; the inner scale reads 0 at the right end of the base and 180 at the left end, so the number n sits at n degrees measured anticlockwise from the right end. The number height is 0.065 R. Radial lines: 17 straight GUIDE lines at 10, 20 ... 170 degrees from the right end, each from radius 0.25 R to radius 0.67 R; the 90-degree line is drawn in INK. Rays: from O draw six rays in INK 4 px, each of length 1.30 R with a small filled INK arrowhead (length 0.05 R) at its tip, at these angles measured anticlockwise from the right end of the base: OP at 0 degrees (along the base to the right), OQ at 35 degrees, OR at 95 degrees, OS at 125 degrees, OT at 160 degrees and OU at 180 degrees (along the base to the left), so P, O and U lie on one horizontal straight line. The rays pass over the scales and leave the protractor. Letters: P, Q, R, S, T and U in INK, each centred at distance 1.43 R from O on its own ray, and the letter O in INK centred at (0, -0.17 R). No other text and no angle arcs. Canvas: 1456 x 816 px card, BG white, R = 400 px; centre the drawing so that its bounding box (x from -1.47 R to +1.47 R, y from -0.22 R to +1.47 R) sits in the middle of the card.

angle arcs, angle names or angle measures between rays

differences of the readings give the 14 LP answers, e.g. QOR = 95 - 35 = 60, QOU = 180 - 35 = 145, TOU = 180 - 160 = 20

items.question_text: Make your own protractor by paper folding. 1. Draw a circle of a convenient radius on a sheet of paper. Cut out the circle (Fig. 2.13). A circle or one full turn is 360°. 2. Fold the semi-circular sheet in half as shown in Fig. 2.15 to form a quarter circle. 4. Fold the sheet again as shown in Figs. 2.16 and 2.17. 5. Continue with another half fold as shown in Fig. 2.18. 6. Unfold and mark the creases as OB, OC, ..., etc., as shown in Fig. 2.19 and Fig. 2.20.
